**Exercises to Help Relieve Spinal Pain**

Spinal pain can affect your daily activities, posture, and overall quality of life. Regular stretching and strengthening exercises can help reduce pain, improve flexibility, and support a healthier spine. However, exercises should always be performed under the guidance of a qualified spine specialist or physiotherapist, especially if the pain is severe or persistent.

Dr. Sagar Khairnar, Orthopaedic Spine Surgeon, recommends gentle, controlled movements to strengthen the muscles supporting the spine and improve mobility. Beneficial exercises may include pelvic tilts, cat-cow stretches, knee-to-chest stretches, bridge exercises, bird-dog exercises, hamstring stretches, and core strengthening exercises. Walking and low-impact activities can also help improve spinal health and reduce stiffness.

Maintain proper posture while sitting and standing, avoid lifting heavy objects incorrectly, and take regular breaks if you work at a desk for long hours. If your spinal pain is accompanied by numbness, weakness, pain radiating to the arms or legs, difficulty walking, or loss of bladder or bowel control, seek immediate medical evaluation.

I visited this orthopedic doctor for persistent pain in my left leg. Initially, I was prescribed medication for 10 days, but there was no improvement. On my follow-up visit, the doctor suggested it could be a nerve-related issue (femoral nerve gliding)

I consulted a neurologist, underwent treatment, and also completed a spine MRI, which showed no nerve-related problems. Despite sharing these results, the orthopedic doctor continued prescribing nerve-related medication without investigating other possible causes. Even after repeated visits and worsening pain, imaging like X-ray or MRI was not advised proactively.

Instead, I was recommended physiotherapy, which unfortunately worsened my condition significantly and led to limping. After nearly two months of ongoing pain and deterioration, I insisted on further investigation. Only then was a hip MRI suggested.

The MRI revealed that I had Stage 2 Avascular Necrosis (AVN) in both hips. Due to the delay in proper diagnosis, I eventually required core decompression surgery.

This experience was very disappointing. Early imaging and a broader diagnostic approach could have identified the issue sooner and potentially reduced the severity of intervention required. I would advise others to seek timely second opinions, especially if symptoms persist without improvement.
